featured_reviews.name: Shrutika Parab
featured_reviews.review_text:
I would like to share some feedback based on my experience on my wedding day.
1. 	The attitude towards my family felt unwelcoming. Family members were not allowed in the makeup room, even when they wanted to offer polite suggestions.
2.	The makeup session took much longer than the suggested 2.5 hours, extending to 3.5 hours. The extra time seemed to be spent focusing on video rcordings for marketing rather than the actual bridal look, which was frustrating.
3.	Client suggestions were not well received. Instead of a friendly discussion, any input from my side was dismissed with a firm "this will look better" response.
4.	I specifically requested the use of high-quality makeup products and even offered to provide my own if needed. While initially Swati agreeing, but she did not use good-quality products on the wedding day. This resulted in a patchy finish, with makeup coming off throughout the event, which was incredibly disappointing.
5.	The makeup technique felt outdated and did not provide the glamorous yet natural look I was hoping for. Proper contouring was missing, which made the overall appearance less refined.
6. 	Bridal makeup should extend to the neck area for a seamless finish, but unfortunately, the service only covered the face, leaving an uneven look. This was not what I expected from a bridal package.
7.    While I appreciate the effort in capturing and sharing my wedding makeup on social media, the video uploaded on Instagram was edited poorly. It made my natural skin appear much worse than it actually is, which was misleading. I have fair, eventoned skin, yet the video made it look patchy and unflattering before the makeup application. Such editing misrepresents reality and does not reflect a professional approach.
While the saree draping was well done, the makeup experience left much to be desired. I hope this feedback helps improve future bridal services for other clients.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
I am genuinely surprised to receive such an extensive list of concerns after almost a full year, especially since no issues were raised on the wedding day, during the event, or even in the weeks that followed. We always encourage brides to share any discomfort immediately so we can address it on the spot. Nevertheless, I will respond to each point you mentioned.
- Regarding your family not being allowed inside the makeup room:
We follow this rule strictly for space management, and to ensure the bride’s comfort. This is communicated to all clients in advance and is standard practice across the industry.
On your wedding date—3rd February 2025—the makeup room provided to us was extremely small, with space for only about three people. There was no proper lighting, dirty mirrors and no AC, and since you were not fully ready with your outfit, allowing additional people inside would not have been appropriate or comfortable for you.
- Regarding the makeup duration:
Bridal makeup requires precision, and occasional delays can happen. However, the claim that more time was spent on recordings is not accurate. Any short clips taken were minimal and never interfered with the quality of work.
It is also important to clarify that you arrived 1.5 hours late. We were scheduled to begin at 7:00 AM, but we could only start around 8:45 AM. We had already reached the venue by 6:30 AM, but the bride had not arrived, which naturally shifted the entire timeline.
- Regarding suggestions not being accepted:
We always discuss the look with the bride beforehand. On the wedding day, the artist may guide the client based on professional expertise, but the intention is never to dismiss anyone’s input. Our team was present at the hall on time, but since you arrived late, the coordination and flow were affected.
- Regarding product quality and video recording:
You had requested high‑quality products, and our kit consists only of branded, professional-grade items. If you had any dissatisfaction with the finish, informing us immediately would have helped greatly instead of raising it after a year.
As for video recording, I always take permission before shooting any clip. If a client is uncomfortable, I do not record at all.
- Regarding makeup style and product usage:
Makeup style preferences vary from bride to bride. The technique used for you was based on the look you approved during the consultation. If you felt it appeared outdated, mentioning it at that time would have allowed us to adjust it.
Your skin was oily and acne-prone on that day, so I used products suitable for that condition, including:
- PAC water‑based moisturizer (ideal for oily skin and summer season)
- Smashbox primer
- LA Girl corrector
- Estée Lauder foundation mixed with Kryolan diluter
- Huda Beauty powder
- Complete skin preparation and finishing products ( Those are nor local products)
- ⁠
Although your package included HD makeup, I upgraded you to airbrush makeup without any additional charge. Every product used was high-end and chosen specifically for your skin type to ensure long-lasting results.
- Regarding neck makeup:
Neck makeup is always done when required and based on the outfit. If you felt it was uneven, mentioning it during the session would have allowed us to correct it instantly.
- Regarding the Instagram video:
No edits are ever done to make anyone’s skin look worse. Raw clips are used to show real transformations. If you felt uncomfortable with the video, informing us at that time would have allowed us to remove it immediately.
I am glad you appreciated the saree draping, but it is disappointing to hear the rest of your concerns only after such a long time. Feedback is most helpful when shared promptly so it can be verified and addressed fairly.
